title: Quantum geometry at arbitrary genus - I: Anharmonic potentials
abstract: In quantum mechanics of genus-1 potentials, perturbation theory around the topologically trivial saddle and non-perturbative instanton saddle are constructively related via the P/NP relation. Whether such a relation persists for higher-genus potentials has remained an open problem. In this work, we resolve it using tools from complex algebraic geometry combined with exact WKB. The classical energy conservation relation $p^2 = 2(E-V(q))$ defines a genus-g Riemann surface $X$, whose periods are naturally organized by its Jacobian variety $J(X) = \mathbb{C}^{\text{g}}/Λ$ via the Abel-Jacobi map, and independently by the solution basis of the associated Picard-Fuchs equations. We show that the physically relevant, WKB-active cycles are generally related to the Picard-Fuchs basis by a linear transformation that lies in $\text{SL}(2\text{g},\mathbb{Z})$ but not in the symplectic group $\text{Sp}(2\text{g},\mathbb{Z})$ once $\text{g}\geq2$, in contrast to the genus-1 case, where the two groups coincide. This mismatch is the obstruction that has made an explicit higher-genus P/NP relation elusive. We show that it can be resolved by passing to a modified Riemann bilinear identity, built from a suitably transformed intersection matrix, which the WKB-active periods do satisfy exactly. The result is an all-orders quantum P/NP relation valid for potentials of arbitrary genus, which we derive explicitly for genus-2 (quintic and sextic) and genus-3 (septic and octic) anharmonic oscillators.
summary: This work tackles the generalization of the P/NP relation in quantum mechanics from simple (genus-1) potentials to complex, higher-genus systems. By employing advanced tools from algebraic geometry and exact WKB theory, the authors overcome a major mathematical obstruction related to the symplectic structure. They successfully derive an all-orders quantum P/NP relation applicable to potentials defining Riemann surfaces of arbitrary genus.
main_problem: The paper aims to generalize the P/NP relation, which connects perturbative and non-perturbative quantum actions, from genus-1 potentials to potentials defining Riemann surfaces of arbitrary genus.
main_result: The authors derive an all-orders quantum P/NP relation valid for arbitrary genus by modifying the Riemann bilinear identity using a suitably transformed intersection matrix.
method: The approach combines complex algebraic geometry (Jacobian varieties, Abel-Jacobi map) with the exact WKB formalism applied to the classical energy conservation relation defining a genus-g Riemann surface.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum mechanical particle governed by a potential V(q) such that the classical energy relation p^2 = 2(E-V(q)) defines a hyperelliptic Riemann surface X of genus g. The analysis focuses on anharmonic oscillators for explicit examples.
key_observables: Quantum periods, WKB-active cycles, and the relationship between the Picard-Fuchs basis and the canonical homology basis.
important_parameters: The genus g of the Riemann surface, and the semiclassical parameter $\hbar$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of a classical energy conservation relation defining the Riemann surface, and the formal structure of the WKB expansion.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the canonical basis cycles and their symplectic intersection properties. Figure 2 shows the Riemann surface structure for a genus-2 example, and Figure 3 relates to the potential profile and WKB analysis.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general framework by relating quantum periods to the geometry of the Riemann surface. It identifies the obstruction to the P/NP relation at $g \geq 2$ (the mismatch between $	ext{SL}(2g, \mathbb{Z})$ and $	ext{Sp}(2g, \mathbb{Z})$) and resolves it by constructing a modified Riemann bilinear identity, culminating in explicit derivations for $g=2$ and $g=3$.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework developed for relating quantum periods across arbitrary genus curves is highly relevant to understanding quantum corrections in integrable systems and quantum field theories where geometry plays a central role.

The squiggly dark red lines indicate the branch cuts emanating from pairs of branch points, and the dashed segments of cycles indicate they lie on the second sheet. This basis set is equivalent to any other choice of canonical basis set up to an Sp(2g, Z) transformation. b, The intersection number structure of two cycles γ1 and γ2. The homology space is endowed with the inner product shown, which gives the space its symplectic structure defined by the intersection matrix (2.6).
